title: A Slack channel message claims a milestone shipped that's still open
author: kwaku-ananse
description: The Slack source's second claims-X leg, alongside slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue (task 599) -- a third leg, slack-message-claims-unmerged-pr, remains open for a future hour. Extracts every 'milestone #N' claim phrase (milestone_claims.py's shared grammar, imported verbatim, the sixth recipe to bind to it) from a Slack channel message's own text and cross-checks it against the live milestone tracker's own state -- the identical milestone-claim check mention-claims-open-milestone already runs against X's own mentions, applied here to the Slack channel-message surface slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue already opened. A milestone that exists but is still open is the seam: a message already sitting in a Slack channel disagrees with GitHub's own record, and nothing on either platform ever compares them. Fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, never a live network call -- the-hand gateway holds a real, connected upstream Slack app but exposes zero Slack-capable tools on its live toolset today, same WIP note slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue already carries.
confidence_notes: Age-gated by hours since the message's own ts, holding slack-message-claims-unfixed-issue's own 0.85/0.5 bar exactly -- not an independently re-reasoned number just because the claim is about a milestone rather than an issue. A Slack channel message is posted once and stands, exactly as durable and readable-later as a tweet or a mention once posted -- mention-claims-open-milestone's/tweet-claims-open-milestone's identical bar applies, not review-comment-claims-open-milestone's lower 0.55/0.85 bar for an editable surface. A claim checked within 24 hours of posting might still be a race (the milestone actually closing out moments after the message went out) rather than a settled public overclaim (0.5, below the 0.70 confidence bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden). At or past 24 hours with the named milestone still open, it is unambiguous (flat 0.85). The check itself is objective, same reasoning as every claims-open-milestone sibling: the claimed milestone's own live state field, verified against ListMilestones, not a guess about which tracker the poster meant. A named milestone that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- a broken reference is a future Slack-side dangling-reference recipe's own seam, not this one's. A named milestone that IS closed is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. A message with no 'milestone #N' claim phrase at all produces no candidate. No text in this recipe's own headline/detail strings ever names or grades the Slack poster -- CONTRIBUTING.md's 'No grading, ever' law, same as every recipe in this engine.
